What is the Editionskompass?

What does Git have to do with scholarly editing?

Are you working on an edition and interested in Git? You are in the right place. The Editionskompass invites you to discover what this tool can offer from the perspective of scholarly editing.

Git is often seen as a technical matter for a project’s IT partners. Yet its use directly concerns editorial work: Git can make decisions and their development traceable, shape collaboration, and open up new ways of publishing and reusing an edition. It can offer much more than version control and data protection.

Using Git also means shaping scholarly working practices. What do we record? Who may read, contribute and approve? Which traces of our work remain, and who can analyse them later? These possibilities bring responsibilities and consequences to consider before introducing the tool.

Four lifelike project examples help you explore these questions and develop a suitable strategy for your edition: on your own, in a team or in a workshop. No technical knowledge is required to begin. Curiosity about Git and your own editorial practice is enough.
